newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Amara Holdings eyes hotel expansion in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Amara Holdings eyes hotel expansion in Asia.

text.p: Soon-to-be-listed Amara Holdings Ltd expects a 16 percent growth in 1997 net profit and a 30 percent growth in turnover, company officials said on Friday.

"Turnover for 1997 is forecast at Singapore $40.3 million, which represents a 30 percent increase over 1996 and profit after tax at S$7.3 million, which represents 16 percent increase over 1996," Eddy See, the group's financial controller, told a news conference during its initial public offer (IPO).
Amara, which invests in hotels, property and food services, is offering 132 million shares at S$0.30 each to raise S$34.2 million for expansion in Singapore and Asia.
For the year ended December 31, 1996, the group's turnover was at S$31.07 million while net profit was at S$6.28 million.
"We seek to widen our earnings base in our regionalisation move," said Albert Teo, the group's chief executive officer.
Expansion strategy for its hotel sector, which accounts for about 78 percent of its earnings, includes acquiring or developing hotels in major Asian gateways, Teo said.
It will be adding 47 new rooms to its flagship 341-room Amara Hotel in Singapore by the end of 1997.
Other hotel investments include a 311-room hotel in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam and plans to open a 239-room hotel in Chengdu, China in 1998 and a 352-room hotel in Shanghai, China in 2000.
Teo said Amara plans to acquire selective properties in Singapore to provide a steady income stream to fund its future expansion.

"In the medium to longer term, the group's growth is expected to arise from the hotel extension, Amara Corporate Tower and its regional hotel investments and operations," Amara said in its prospectus.
According to See, Amara Hotel in Singapore has enjoyed above industry average room yields.
While profit per room for Amara Hotel was around $19,000 as of December 1996, its competitors like Hotel Plaza and Republic Hotel were only reaping S$11,000 and S$16,000 respectively.
